parts.instructions: Answer these questions about communication and technology.
questions: How do you usually keep in touch with your friends and family?
How much time do you spend using a computer or smartphone every day?
What do you think is the most useful form of technology in your daily life?
Do you prefer communicating by phone or by text message? Why?
Have you ever used email to communicate in English? How was that experience?

cueCard.topic: Describe a time when you learned to use a new piece of technology.
bullets: why you needed to learn it
how you learned to use it
and explain how you felt about learning this new technology

questions: How has technology changed the way people learn languages compared to the past?
Do you think schools should provide students with computers or tablets? Why or why not?
What are the disadvantages of relying too much on technology for communication?
How do you think communication technology will develop in the next 20 years?
Is it true that older generations find it harder to adapt to new technology? Why do you think that is?
Do you believe that technology can ever fully replace face-to-face communication?

_legacyTask.title: Electronic Mail
_legacyTask.scenario: You are studying at a language school and have heard that students may obtain an electronic mail (e-mail) address so that they can send and receive messages by computer.
_legacyTask.role: The Examiner is the Student Services advisor.
topicsToAsk: how to obtain an e-mail address

interviewerNotes.description: Information for the Examiner: responses to the candidate's questions
prompts: what e-mail is: means by which to send messages from one computer to another over the telephone lines
cost: free for students at this language school
how to obtain an e-mail address: complete an application form and return to Student Services
location of e-mail at school: in the independent learning centre or computer laboratory
equipment needed at home: a modem and a telephone line
courses on e-mail: Friday afternoon classes throughout the year

parts.instructions: Answer these questions about music and entertainment.
questions: What kind of music do you like to listen to? Why?
How often do you go to concerts or live music events?
Do you prefer listening to music alone or with other people?
Have you ever played a musical instrument? Which one?
What role does music play in your daily life?

cueCard.topic: Describe a concert or live performance you have attended or would like to attend.
bullets: what kind of event it was or would be
where it took or would take place
who you went or would go with
and explain why it was or would be memorable

parts.topic: The Music Industry and Live Events
questions: Do you think live concerts are still popular in the age of streaming music? Why?
How has the music industry changed in the last few decades?
Should the government provide more funding for the arts and live performances?
Why do some people prefer recorded music over live performances?
How important are music festivals for a country's culture and tourism?
Do you think musical taste changes as people get older? Why?

_legacyTask.title: Concert
_legacyTask.scenario: Find out as much as possible about a concert your examiner has been to recently.
_legacyTask.role: The candidate asks the examiner about a concert they attended.
topicsToAsk: transport to and from the concert

interviewerNotes.description: Information for the Examiner: responses to the candidate's questions about the concert
prompts: the type of concert / the location: rock/folk/jazz/classical, city stadium
the cost: $55/£25
transport to and from the concert: bus (hard to park car)
the audience: 500-1,000 people, lots of audience participation
the length of the concert: 3 hours
his/her opinion of the concert: really enjoyed it

parts.instructions: Answer these questions about nature and the environment.
questions: Do you enjoy spending time outdoors in nature? Why or why not?
What do you personally do to help protect the environment?
Have you ever participated in any environmental activities or events?
Is the natural environment where you live well protected?
What is the most serious environmental problem in your country?

cueCard.topic: Describe an environmental group, club, or initiative you know about.
bullets: what the group or initiative is called
and explain why you think their work is important

questions: Do you think individuals or governments have a greater responsibility to protect the environment?
How effective are environmental groups in influencing government policy?
What more could schools do to educate young people about environmental issues?
Do you think the environment is better or worse than it was 50 years ago?
Should companies be forced to pay for the pollution they create?
What can ordinary people do in their daily lives to reduce their environmental impact?

_legacyTask.title: An Environmental Group
_legacyTask.scenario: You are interested in joining a group of students at the university who work to protect the environment.
_legacyTask.role: The examiner provides information about the environmental group.

interviewerNotes.description: Information for the Examiner: responses to the candidate's questions
prompts: the name of the group: Green Action
action that they take: planting trees, clearing up rubbish
the cost of membership: $10/£5 a year
what members have to do: participate in two events (organised by the group) a year
number of members: 4,500
when the group was founded: 1996

parts.instructions: Answer these questions about books and reading.
questions: Do you enjoy reading books? What kind of books do you read?
How often do you buy books? Where do you usually buy them?
Do you prefer reading books in your own language or in English? Why?
What was the last book you read? Did you enjoy it?
Do you think reading books is more beneficial than watching videos for learning? Why or why not?

cueCard.topic: Describe a book that you found very useful.
bullets: how you found out about this book
and explain why you found it so useful

questions: Do you think self-study is as effective as studying in a classroom?
How important are textbooks in the modern classroom?
What qualities make a good educational book?
How has technology changed the way people learn languages?
Is it better to study alone or with a teacher? Why?
Will digital books completely replace printed textbooks in the future?

_legacyTask.title: Buying a Book
_legacyTask.scenario: Your teacher recommended a good English language writing book to assist students with their written work.
_legacyTask.role: The examiner provides information about the recommended book.

interviewerNotes.description: Information for the Examiner: responses to the candidate's questions about the book
prompts: the level of the book: It is valuable for students preparing for university entrance and for advanced learners of English.
the title: "Writing Academic English" or another text you know of
the authors: by Walton and Hague
the cost: around $40/£20
place of purchase: Name a suitable bookshop in the town.
extras — cassettes, answers: There is no cassette as it is only a writing book. It does not provide answers, but the teacher could help with corrections.
